Sarah — thanks for the clear ask and the questionnaire. High level answers up front, followed by a short matrix attached (redaction-matrix.xlsx) and next steps.

High-level summary:
- Retention defaults (hosted pilot): request/response payloads (30 days), KV cache + model state: 7 days by default (configurable down to 0), audit logs (90 days). These are our hosted defaults for new pilot tenants; Dedicated/Private deployments can be set to customer-specified SLAs.
- Redaction options: we support server-side field-level redaction at ingestion via schema-based rules (keys/regex), and automatic prefix/PII tokenization for common patterns (SSN, credit card). For PHI, we recommend a joint approach: client-side de-identification for high-sensitivity fields plus server-side structural redaction for transit and cache.
- Proof of deletion: we provide deletion job receipts and a purge log showing object ids and deletion timestamps. For hosted pilots we can provide a signed attestation (pdf) and S3 lifecycle purge records on request.

I'll paste more details below for the specific questionnaire items. Looping in Karthik for config/limits and Rishi for example redaction schemas.

Sarah, Marissa,

Quick technical clarifications per the questionnaire:
1) Token/log retention: tokens from generation (input+output) are stored transiently for inference accounting and caching. Default retention is 30 days; customers may request shorter windows for pilots. Token-level analytics (for cost breakdown) are derived from ephemeral records and not linked to raw PII unless the payload contains it.

2) KV cache: KV is isolated per tenant. Default TTL is 7 days; we can set KV TTL to 0 (no caching) for Harbor's pilot if you need no persisted state. Note: disabling KV will increase per-token latency/cost for repeated contexts.

3) Field-level redaction: we have two server-side mechanisms — a) ingestion redactors: rule-based (key names + regex) that replace matched substrings with a hash or redact token, and b) schema-driven filters that drop entire fields before storage. These run before any persistence.

4) PHI handling: for data classified as PHI we recommend: client-side tokenization or pseudonymization for direct identifiers, plus server-side structural redaction for narrative fields. We can ship a sample transform library (python snippet) you can run pre-ingest.

5) Deletion and attestations: delete jobs are run asynchronously against tenant objects; we provide a job id, the object ids deleted, and timestamps. For pilot customers we can provide a signed deletion attestation and an S3 bucket purge manifest when data was stored in S3. For full Private deployments we support HSM-backed key destruction as an additional control.

Attachment: I attached a short redaction schema example in the matrix for common Harbor fields — let me know if any specific field names need mapping to your schema.

Sarah — quick answers:
- 0-day retention for request/response payloads: Yes, for a scoped test group we can configure tenant-level retention to 0 days. In practice this means we do not write payloads to persistent storage; ephemeral in-memory logs for the inference pipeline may exist for seconds to minutes while the request completes, but nothing is persisted beyond that. We'll document the exact flow and trade-offs (no historical debugging, increased sampling complexity).

- Purge logs: purge/delete job receipts are retained for 365 days by default to support audit requests; they are stored hashed and access-controlled. If Harbor requires shorter retention for the purge receipts themselves, we can set that to 90 days for the pilot. We do not keep immutable copies beyond customer-configured retention unless required for legal holds.

- Redaction preview: we have a small internal preview endpoint and a transform library we can run against a sample dataset. We'll provide instructions and a one-hour workshop to validate transforms against your sample extracts.
